mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 3% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in CPIAUCSL above 3% and FEDFUNDS below 2% for two consecutive months signals a disconnect between inflation and policy rates, creating uncertainty that drives higher equity volatility and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% AND FEDFUNDS < 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A consistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above the prior year's average, combined with a flat or declining GDP (GDPC1), signals elevated precautionary savings and weak aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > previous year average AND GDPC1 monthly change <= 0 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in monthly payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 250k for three consecutive months signals a strong labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 250000 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both INDPRO and HOUST of more than 0.4% signals a broad-based contraction in manufacturing and housing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.4% AND HOUST monthly change < -0.4%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered months.
